subject: ventures/quick-pick-survey
auditor: agent session (Claude), 2026-11-19 sample round, independent quality subagent
professional: a survey methodologist / market researcher who runs paired-comparison and MaxDiff (best-worst scaling) studies, with a Bayesian statistician as second reader: first checks are that the Bradley-Terry and best-worst likelihoods and their intervals match the published models, that the rank ranges and 'chance of being the favourite' are calibrated, that the team (random-effects) read is honest about disagreement, and that every 'measured' number on the page traces to a reproducible run

evidence.correctness: Seven outputs recomputed independently, all agree. Scripts in the session scratchpad (qa/recompute.mjs, qa/indep.py, qa/t.ts, qa/indep2.py), Python 3.13 with numpy+scipy. (1) Browser Bradley-Terry refit (site/rank-core.mjs fit -> engine/btRefit.mjs refitRatings) on 10 picks over 4 options incl. one tie: mu 1.713962 / -0.142166 / -0.729576 / -0.842220 and posterior variances 2.037086 / 1.404612 / 1.548765 / 1.653577; my scipy BFGS MAP of sum log sigmoid with N(0, (350/173.7178)^2) prior and tie as half a win each way, plus finite-difference Hessian inverse, gives the same to 6 digits. (2) chanceAbove = Phi(diff/sd(diff)): 0.908076 and 0.536988, identical with scipy norm.cdf. (3) Sequential best-worst (MaxDiff) model (site/best-worst.mjs) on three 4-option screens: mu 1.337871 / 0.758432 / -0.766563 / -1.329740, identical to my own softmax-best then softmax-worst-of-rest likelihood. (4) DerSimonian-Laird pool (src/lib/groupRanking.ts) on 5 respondents not in its tests: 1543.13899 / 46.21655 / 74.87049, identical to textbook DL by hand. (5) Glicko-2 rating-period example (updateGlickoPeriod) 1464.0507 / 151.5165 / 0.0599960, matching my from-scratch Glickman (2013) steps 1-8 and the paper's 1464.06/151.52/0.05999. (6) fairCoinTail(30,24) 1.43090636e-3 and (13,2) 2.24609375e-2, identical to 2*scipy binom.cdf. (7) how-many-pairwise-comparisons page: n(n-1)/2 = 190/435/780/1225 and ceil(log2 n!) = 62/108/160/215 for n = 20/30/40/50 all match lgamma; '93 picks, 0.94 vs 0.95 Spearman at 20' matches docs/picks-needed-2026-11-14.jsonl (93.3, 0.935, 0.947). Also re-ran `node scripts/rank-range-coverage.mjs --n 15 --spreads 1.5 --runs 12 --seed 2000` (9 s): the row reproduces the committed jsonl bit for bit (fixed cover 0.8, own 0.961). Held at 3, not 4: in that same row the 'chance of being the favourite' shown at the own prior is 0.40 while the shown favourite was the true one 2 times in 12 (0.167), so the favourite chance is still over-confident for close-call answerers (12 runs, wide interval; RANK-PAGE.md says it still overclaims for ordinary answerers on 15). Not recomputed: question selection, the Postgres routes, decide.html's graded model.

evidence.verification: `cd site && node --test '*.test.mjs'`: 124 tests, 124 pass, 3.9 s. `npx vitest run --config vitest.fast.config.ts`: 50 files, 521 tests, all pass, 28 s (up from 304 at the 2026-11-10 audit). Six seeded mutations with platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: the three that survived on 2026-11-10 are now caught (Glicko newMu x0.9 caught by glicko2.test.ts; DL (q-(k-1)) -> (q-k) caught by groupRanking.test.ts; plus Davidson pinned probabilities now in conjoint.test.ts:173-191, not re-mutated); new mutants: rank-core diffVar dropping the -2cov term caught; btRefit.ts prior precision halved caught; but two in the MaxDiff likelihood (site/best-worst.mjs) survived: the worst tap read over the whole screen instead of the rest after the best (a different, non-sequential model), and the pair-tie weight 0.5 -> 0.6 in answerTerms. best-worst.test.mjs checks the gradient against finite differences of its own log likelihood and that a 2-screen equals one pick, but never pins the 4-option likelihood or fit to a closed-form value, so a wrong model is self-consistent and passes. 4 of 6 caught.

Good: generated engine with a --check and a test that fails when stale (one engine, not a copy); log-space softmax; Cholesky with an explicit 'not positive definite' error; refitRatings rejects answers naming unknown ids instead of dropping them; erf approximation documented with its error bound; reasons and measurements written next to each constant. Still standing from 2026-11-10: invertMatrix nudges a singular pivot by 1e-8 rather than surfacing it (src/lib/conjoint.ts:161); MIN_RD 30 floor feeds back into later Glicko updates (src/lib/glicko2.ts:102). rank-core.mjs is ~980 lines and the README/llms.txt carry very long change-log paragraphs (README.md:222 is one 1,500-character line), which a reviewer would ask to move to docs.

evidence.fitness: Job: a team lead ranks 20 options with 10 colleagues. Now possible without deploying anything: paste the list into rank.html, share the # link, each person answers in the browser (about 93 picks for 20 options at ordinary consistency, measured in simulation), sends back a QP1 code, the lead pastes codes and gets a team order with group and population 90% rank ranges, agreement, and a CSV. I drove the same engine headless for one person (8 options, 48 picks, sensible order, code round-trip, CSV). A solo user can also do a MaxDiff-style best/worst or a weighted decision matrix (decide.html). Limits: no outside user yet; picks per person are high for long lists (about 1.6x for top-k); I did not load the page in a real browser here; the self-hosted Postgres app was not run.
evidence.domain: Compared against Bradley-Terry / Thurstone paired comparison (David 1988), sequential best-worst scaling (Marley & Louviere 2005), DerSimonian-Laird random effects, and Glickman's Glicko-2. The 2026-11-10 objection (a time-varying Glicko-2 used for static preferences) is largely answered: the per-person results and the rank page now come from a full-likelihood Bayesian Bradley-Terry refit with a Laplace covariance and an empirical-Bayes prior sd, which is what a methodologist would choose, and the btRefit header argues the likelihood principle for the adaptive design correctly. MaxDiff is read with the exact sequential best-worst model instead of five implied pairs, the right call. The team read separates 'this group' (mean of posteriors) from a random-effects 'population' with marginal-likelihood tau, which is principled. Departures: Laplace approximation on few picks per item, and the favourite chance remains over-confident for near-coin-flip answerers (reproduced row above); calibration evidence rests on 12-24 simulated people per row and on logistic answerers, plus Thurstone off-model checks; no real-respondent validation beyond PrefLib replays (scripts/preflib.ts, not run here); position-bias handling is randomisation plus a run test, not a measured bias estimate.

defects.what: The MaxDiff (best-worst) likelihood is not pinned to a closed-form value: reading the worst tap over the whole screen instead of the rest after the best (a different model), and changing the tie weight in answerTerms, both pass all 124 site tests. Tests check gradient vs finite differences of the same likelihood and the 2-option reduction only. A 4-option screen's log likelihood and one small fit (e.g. the qa values in this audit: mu 1.337871 / 0.758432 / -0.766563 / -1.329740) would pin it.

'Chance of being the favourite' is still over-confident for near-coin-flip answerers: re-running the author's own coverage script for 15 options, spread 1.5, the own-prior table showed 0.40 while the favourite was right 2 times in 12. RANK-PAGE.md admits an overclaim for ordinary answerers; the page does not tell the person.

'randomises which option appears on top, so screen position cannot bias the result' overstates randomisation (removes systematic bias in expectation; a respondent's position lean still adds noise). Unchanged since the 2026-11-10 audit.

invertMatrix silently nudges a singular pivot by 1e-8, so a degenerate conjoint Hessian gives arbitrary standard errors with no flag; MIN_RD 30 floor is fed back into later Glicko updates. Unchanged since 2026-11-10.
'log2(n!) comparisons, about n log2 n: 62 for 20 items': n log2 n is 86 at n=20, so the gloss misleads a reader; log2(n!) ~ n log2 n - 1.44 n.

README 'How it works' still says Glicko-2 RD gives every ranking 'a real confidence interval', though the shown intervals now come from the Bradley-Terry refit (btRefit.ts, insights route); llms.txt still has two '## Pages' headings.

verdict: Re-audit nine days after the 2026-11-10 audit (which failed on verification and claims). The fixes held: the three mutants that survived then (Glicko update, DerSimonian-Laird tau, Davidson tie) are now pinned and two of them were re-seeded and caught; the chess.com claim and the misnamed Glicko test are fixed; llms.txt points at the served host. The product has also grown a no-install browser ranker whose maths I recomputed independently: Bayesian Bradley-Terry MAP and Laplace variances, pairwise chances, the sequential best-worst model, DL pooling, Glickman's example, the binomial run tail and the page's comparison counts all agree with my own scipy code to 6 digits, and a committed simulation row reproduced bit for bit. 645 tests pass (521 vitest fast + 124 site), typecheck and lint clean, the generated engine is current. It meets the bar at 3 across the board (finished, completeness 3), not 4: the new MaxDiff likelihood is self-consistent but unpinned (two seeded model changes survived), the favourite chance is still over-confident for near-coin-flip answerers, the position-bias sentence and an 'about n log2 n' gloss overstate, and there is still no outside user, real-browser run, Postgres integration run or next build in this audit. Earlier defects still standing: position-bias wording, invertMatrix nudge, MIN_RD feedback, duplicate llms.txt heading.
